subject: Urgent: evening batch p99 spike impacting VectorMed long-window requests
messages:
From: Jae Park <jae.park@vectormed.com>
To: support@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@vectormed.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 03:14:00 -0700
Subject: p99 spike on evening batch — long-window jobs

Hi Redwood support team,

We started seeing a large jump in p99 latency during our nightly ingestion/summary batch that kicked off ~22:30 PT last night. Summary: p95 moved from ~220ms -> ~1.0s, p99 from ~650ms -> ~4.8s; error rate rose from 0.18% to 1.6% and throughput dropped ~12%. The jobs are multi-document summarization requests and some requests hit longer context windows (8k-16k tokens).

Attached are a small log bundle and a CSV with p50/p95/p99 by minute. Can you confirm if anything changed on your side (model rollout, kernel changes, routing)? We need a timeline — these batches power customer-facing reports.

Thanks,
Jae
Ops Lead | VectorMed
attachments: vectormed_evening_p99_spike_logs_0915.zip, p99_report_20270914.csv

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Jae Park <jae.park@vectormed.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 03:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: p99 spike on evening batch — long-window jobs

Hi Jae — thanks for the alert and the attachments. We're prioritizing this. Quick notes and next steps:
- We're ingesting the logs now.
- Marcus (infra) will validate if any model variants or kernel changes rolled last night.
- Dylan (support) will trace a representative request from the CSV to see if KV-cache behavior or batching anomalies are present.
- Can you confirm the typical token distribution: mostly 8k with ~5% hitting 16k, or are you seeing more heavy tails? If you can drop a couple of exact request IDs from the CSV that spike at p99 that would help.

Temporary mitigation options we may apply with your consent: route long-context requests to a dedicated pool, or enforce a soft token cap for the evening batch. We'll outline tradeoffs once we have the trace.

I will keep you posted every 30–60 minutes until this is stabilized.

— Stephanie
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 03:39:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: p99 spike on evening batch — long-window jobs

Looking at the initial bundle — no platform-wide rollout recorded in the window. My immediate asks:
1) Provide two full request payloads (one typical 8k and one p99 16k) so I can repro locally and check kernel execution time.
2) Confirm model id + quantization/precision used.

Initial hypothesis: this smells like an increased frequency of KV-cache misses + larger per-step kernel cost for the 16k slices which magnifies at p99 when batching is thin. Immediate mitigation we can flip:
- Route requests with context > 12k into the dedicated long-window pool (few-second config change).
- Enable aggressive prefix caching for VectorMed's tenant for next 24h.

I can push the routing rule now if Ops approves. Running the reproducer locally and will ping with timings.

— Marcus
Director, Infrastructure
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
attachments: none

From: Jae Park <jae.park@vectormed.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 04:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: p99 spike on evening batch — long-window jobs

Stephanie / Marcus — thanks. I've uploaded two redacted request samples in the bundle (request_samples_8k-16k.txt) and highlighted the p99 rows in p99_report_20270914.csv. Token distribution for the batch: ~78% <=8k, ~17% between 8k–16k, ~5% ~16k-18k (multi-doc windows). Model: open-model-v2-large (q4_0).

Timeline: we need something in the next 4 hours — the nightly reports go out 02:00–03:00 UTC and customers will notice. If routing to a dedicated pool reduces throughput we still prefer stable latency over intermittent spikes.

-Jae

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Jae Park <jae.park@vectormed.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 05:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: p99 spike on evening batch — long-window jobs

Update from initial traces (SUP-4127 created):
- Observed KV cache miss rate spike coincident with p99 minutes; for long-context requests we see per-token CPU/GPU kernel time increase non-linearly past ~10k context.
- Batching dropped during those minutes (fewer concurrent long-context jobs), which increases per-request overhead and moves p99 up.
- Error rate increase tied to a small subset of requests hitting a library retry path — we've captured the stack for those.

Immediate actions I recommend (and can enact now):
1) Add tenant-specific routing: all requests with predicted context > 12k -> long-window pool (reduces cross-tenant interference).
2) Enable aggressive prefix caching for VectorMed for 48h.
3) Temporarily set a soft max_tokens cap on summarization endpoint for the nightly job with a 5% fallback to smaller-model variant.

If we get approval, I'll apply 1 & 2 now and open a hotfix branch for the batching/kernel tuning. Estimated p99 improvement: to ~1.0–1.3s immediately, longer-term fix for kernel selection in 7–10 days.

— Dylan
Support Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jae Park <jae.park@vectormed.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 06:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: p99 spike on evening batch — long-window jobs

Folks — I'm proposing we approve the immediate mitigations (tenant routing + prefix caching + soft cap with fallback) and offer VectorMed a 48-hour credit for the impact window. Jae, would you accept that as a short-term remediation?

Neha / Laura — this will touch capacity (dedicated long-window pool) and may require short-term reallocation of reserved capacity for an evening window. Approving now will let Marcus flip the rules and give VectorMed stability before their next nightly job.

If Neha signs off I will send a short note to VectorMed confirming our plan and timeline.

— Stephanie

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jae Park <jae.park@vectormed.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: p99 spike on evening batch — long-window jobs

Neha — approved verbally via Slack, pushed routing rule at 11:42 PT and enabled tenant prefix caching at 11:45 PT. Applied soft cap with fallback to open-model-v2-medium for summarization endpoint during the 23:00–03:00 PT nightly window.

Immediate measured impact: p95 now ~320ms, p99 ~1.10s for the last hour; error rate back down to 0.22%. Throughput restored to ~97% of baseline. Attached a short CSV with post-mitigation metrics.

Action items:
- Dylan: continue root cause work on KV cache behavior and kernel selection; aim for kernel tuning hotfix in 7–10 days.
- Marcus: schedule capacity for long-window pool if VectorMed wants this permanently.
- Stephanie: coordinate customer comms and confirm credit.

— Marcus
Director, Infrastructure
attachments: post_mitigation_metrics_0915.csv
